{{Short description|Closure operator}}
In [[topology]], a '''preclosure operator''' or '''Čech closure operator''' is a [[function (mathematics)|map]] between subsets of a set, similar to a [[topological closure|topological closure operator]], except that it is not required to be [[idempotent]]. That is, a preclosure operator obeys only three of the four [[Kuratowski closure axioms]].

== Definition ==
A preclosure operator on a set <math>X</math> is a map <math>[\ \ ]_p</math>

:<math>[\ \ ]_p:\mathcal{P}(X) \to \mathcal{P}(X)</math>

where <math>\mathcal{P}(X)</math> is the [[power set]] of <math>X.</math>

The preclosure operator has to satisfy the following properties:
# <math> [\varnothing]_p = \varnothing \! </math> (Preservation of nullary [[union (set theory)|unions]]);
# <math> A \subseteq [A]_p </math> (Extensivity);
# <math> [A \cup B]_p = [A]_p \cup [B]_p</math> (Preservation of binary unions).

The last axiom implies  the following:

: 4. <math>A \subseteq B</math> implies <math>[A]_p \subseteq [B]_p</math>.

==Topology==
A set <math>A</math> is '''closed''' (with respect to the preclosure) if <math>[A]_p=A</math>.  A set <math>U \subset X</math> is '''open''' (with respect to the preclosure) if its [[complement (set theory)|complement]] <math>A = X \setminus U</math> is closed. The collection of all open sets generated by the preclosure operator is a [[topological space|topology]];<ref>Eduard Čech, Zdeněk Frolík, Miroslav Katětov, ''Topological spaces'' Prague: Academia, Publishing House of the Czechoslovak Academy of
Sciences, 1966, Theorem 14 A.9 [https://eudml.org/doc/277000].</ref> however, the above topology does not capture the notion of convergence associated to the operator, one should consider a [[pretopological space|pretopology]], instead.<ref>S. Dolecki, ''An Initiation into Convergence Theory'', in F. Mynard, E. Pearl (editors), ''Beyond Topology'',
AMS, Contemporary Mathematics, 2009.
</ref>

==Examples==
===Premetrics===
Given <math>d</math> a [[premetric]] on <math>X</math>, then

:<math>[A]_p = \{x \in X : d(x,A)=0\}</math>

is a preclosure on <math>X.</math>

===Sequential spaces===
The [[sequential closure]] operator <math>[\ \ ]_\text{seq}</math> is a preclosure operator. Given a topology <math>\mathcal{T}</math> with respect to which the sequential closure operator is defined, the [[topological space]] <math>(X,\mathcal{T})</math> is a [[sequential space]] if and only if the topology <math>\mathcal{T}_\text{seq}</math> generated by <math>[\ \ ]_\text{seq}</math> is equal to <math>\mathcal{T},</math> that is, if <math>\mathcal{T}_\text{seq} = \mathcal{T}.</math>
